fair_value_reason: P/E leg (60%): NTM adjusted EPS at 2027-10-09 = 0.31 x FY28 $19.95 ($20.78 consensus x 0.96) + 0.69 x FY29 $22.14 (+11%) = $21.46; x 15.0x (judgment, cut from 16x after the citation gate; see post_gate_decisions) = $322. On the gate-derived multiples 15x is ~17.5% below MTZ's 18.18x NTM consensus P/E (15 / 18.18 = 0.825), ~18% below the 18.36x telecom-core (MTZ, PRIM) average and ~32% below the 22.01x 7-peer median; because the EPS it is applied to is 4% below consensus it equals 14.4x on the unhaircut EPS path, ~21% below MTZ like for like (14.4 / 18.18 = 0.792). EV/EBITDA leg (40%): FY28 EBITDA $8.58B x 14.2% = $1.218B; FY29 +9% = $1.328B; NTM = 0.31 x 1.218 + 0.69 x 1.328 = $1.294B; x 9.5x (judgment, cut from 10x so that the leg matches the 15x P/E) = EV $12.29B (~10.1x FY28E, ~20% below MTZ's 12.57x EV on its $1,600M 2026 guide), less lease-inclusive horizon net debt of $2.56B ($2.33B notional + $0.229B operating leases) = $9.73B / 30.2M shares = $322. Blend 0.6 x 322 + 0.4 x 322 = $322 (estimate). The forecasters' fair values (mean $337) move to ~$338 after my round-2 corrections: agent_4 ~$343 (EV leg at 10x NTM), agent_1 ~$337 (FCF leg removed), agents 2, 3 and 5 unchanged within $1 (buyback fix per-share neutral). All five keep 16x, so the reconciled value is ~5% below that corrected mean, and the gap is the multiple judgment alone. All inputs are verified at the Q2 release, the 10-Q, XBRL and StockAnalysis consensus (re-opened by the citation gate 2026-10-12); the multiples, haircut and FY29 growth are judgment.
supervisor_summary: Dycom at $269 (13.7x NTM consensus EPS vs MasTec 18.2x) has de-rated while FY28 consensus held at $20.78. The FY27 Communications cut was ~$150M of wireless deferral and ~$10M underlying, but cash quality is weaker than reported because supplier finance went from $0 to $367M in a year. Round-2 checks found the agents' remaining disputes small and offsetting: a new $150M buyback exists, the 3.50x covenant is only an incurrence cap, agent_4's trailing EV/EBITDA was too generous, and agent_1 double-counted cash quality. Reconciled fair value is ~$322 (15x NTM EPS $21.46; 9.5x NTM EBITDA). After the citation gate, 16x was only ~12% below MasTec's 18.18x, less than the leverage, cash-quality and concentration reasons support, so I cut it (post_gate_decisions). That puts fair value ~5% below the corrected agent mean of ~$338; the mean ladder (P>=269 = 0.58) was not re-fitted in this step, and confidence stays low. The decisive event is the early-March 2027 FY28 outlook, and the Q3 10-Q in late November is the first read on whether the supplier-finance build unwinds.
key_drivers: Is H2 FY27 Communications flatness timing or a cycle peak? The FY27 Communications midpoint fell $160M (May $6.115B -> Aug $5.955B), of which ~$150M is a stated wireless deferral into FY28 and ~$10M is underlying, and the margin outlook flipped from 'modest improvement' to 'slight decline'. The early-March 2027 FY28 outlook decides it.

The fall was a de-rating, not an estimate cut. FY28 consensus is still $20.78 (11 analysts). DY trades at 13.7x NTM consensus EPS against MTZ at 18.2x and a 7-peer median of 22.0x (gate-derived), and a persistent discount to MTZ (15x NTM P/E, ~17.5% below MTZ's 18.18x and ~21% below it on the unhaircut EPS path; 9.5x NTM EV/EBITDA, ~10.1x FY28E, ~20% below MTZ's 12.57x current-year multiple) is justified by leverage (2.82x vs 2.12x lease-inclusive net debt / company-adjusted TTM EBITDA; 3.20x for DY if the $367.4M supplier-finance balance is counted as debt), concentration and cash quality.

Cash quality and leverage: notional net debt $2,502.6M, and supplier-finance obligations went $0 -> $367.4M in 12 months (FY26 AP +$223.2M). H1 FY27 FCF was -$54.2M. The Q3 10-Q (late Nov) shows whether the build continues or unwinds. A new $150M buyback (through Feb-2028) is available but small.

Carrier concentration: AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4%, Lumen 5.3% of Q2 revenue. Verizon guides 2026 capex down $0.5-1bn while AT&T targets 40M fiber locations by end-2026 and 60M by 2030. The SpaceX-Grain 800 MHz deal hit carriers and lifted towers, a mixed read.
Rates: Kalshi/Polymarket price a ~73% chance of a December hike, a headwind for levered, de-rated contractors.
